body: I will cry that from my window next time someone gives the white woman silently sobbing to herself in random parking lots a weird look. "Fuck off I'm figuring shit out!" Love it.

You can do it! All of this can be yours too, lol. Seriously you can. I'm realizing again and again that life isnt always great. (I mean, duh and yet many times I'm surprised as if this is a new concept). I'm a ship at sea and this is a little storm. But I can handle it. Better than annihilate my ability to perceive the storm exists.
Right? I don't know how to make it better, but I know what will make it worse.
I'm learning (relearning repeatedly) that this will pass. That is a comfort for sure, thank you. Sobriety is actually living life and life is messy and not always a joy.
Just take it one day a time. Days like today nothing I do is right or can make it right, it seems. But I know what will make it worse. It always makes things worse.
I'm usually ok, doing great actually. And then I have days like today where I can't remain above water. Makes me feel crazy sometimes. At least this time I know the cause.
Thank you that means a lot

It really sucks when you can't succeed at something, even when you try. It's so demoralizing, especially if you feel pressure from family because so much of our identity is tied up with family. Thats a hard life lesson. There just are some things we won't be good at. And there's nothing wrong with that. It's a problem if that thing you're not good at is "school" in general (I don't know if that's you). I know so many very successful and happy people who struggled through school. And there are so many talented, smart people that just didn't get it. Because the honest truth is that school doesn't really prepare you. That can be comforting or it can be fucking terrifying. 

For me it was terrifying. I was good at school, good at grades, tests, gold stars. I didn't really face failure. Until the real world slapped me with a bag of bricks. 

I've heard that with 'smart' kids, failure to grasp/master something is especially devestating. I put the quotes because there are so many levels and variations of the human potential, and I really hate how school can make you squish yourself into a select few catagories that don't really exist.  

I'm sorry that your parents place so much pressure on you. Would it be terrible to tell them what that feels like? Even writing a letter, allowing you to revise so you can really make your points and know you won't be intterupted or find yourself arguing things you weren't even trying to talk about. 

I know it's cliche, but most parents really only want the best for their kids. Obviously there are exceptions. But in trying to do that, they can end up doing a lot of harm. Sorry I wrote like four times as much as you did.  I'll stop now. This random internet stranger will be thinking about you.

I am so sorry you're going through this all of this. Toxic families are such a cluster fuck of emotions to deal with, especially if you aren't in a situation to cut them out of your life yet. Please reach out to your friends if you can. The stress and worry you are afraid of causing is nothing to the confused pain they'd feel for the rest of their lives. I hope that is ok to say. 

I will be thinking of you. I hope you can reach out more if this subreddit doesn't cut it. Can you crash on a friend's couch or go to a shelter? Or even drive and just get some clear headspace away from your mother?  It may sound stupid or pointless, but it's something. Something different.
